subject: Mixed-mode endpoint: first-token and sustained throughput carveout for VectorPay pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@vectorpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Mixed-mode endpoint: first-token and sustained throughput carveout for VectorPay pilot

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great alignment on the feature set for the pilot. Per our conversation I wanted to put a short, actionable proposal on the table for the endpoint behaviour we're recommending for VectorPay so your engineering/procurement teams can review.

Summary (proposal):
- Streaming path: used for short, interactive flows (expected completion < 512 tokens). Target TTFT (time-to-first-token) on Dedicated capacity: 150 ms median per our performance profile. Sustained token/sec expectation not guaranteed for microbursts but typical observed 200-350 tok/s depending on sequence length.
- Non-streaming fallback: for long completions (>= 512 tokens) we recommend a synchronous path to avoid instability in interleaved streaming. Proposed commitments: TTFT (initial server response for non-streaming) 700-900 ms; sustained emission rate: 100-140 tokens/sec once generation begins.
- Carveout ask: VectorPay requests the streaming TTFT guarantee for all endpoints regardless of completion length. We can agree to a mixed-mode SLA for the pilot: standard streaming SLA for <512 tokens; for longer responses we offer the non-streaming fallback SLA above and an explicit canary period to measure real traffic patterns.

Attached: VectorPay_Pilot_Perf_Reqs.xlsx (your perf targets) — please see sheet "Targets". I've also attached our redwood-sla-exception-form.xlsx to capture any formal carveouts.

Next steps: can you confirm acceptance of the mixed-mode approach, or indicate which specific points you need redlined? If agreeable, we propose a 2-week canary (1M tokens/day cap) to validate TTFT + sustained rates before locking the pilot SLA.

Thanks,

Ben Carter

Ben,

Appreciate the clear summary. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we push this to procurement/infra:

1) For the non-streaming fallback you list 700-900 ms TTFT — is that measured from request arrival to the first byte of the completion, or from request arrival to the first token returned to client (i.e., after your proxy)? We need the number that's observable from our side (client-to-first-token).
2) The sustained emission rate of 100-140 tok/s: does that include rate-limiting we should expect when the system is operating under high concurrency (50+ concurrent requests)?

We'll attach our internal perf targets (we also included p99 TTFT targets). Can you also include an attachment with proposed contract language we can hand to legal?

-Maria
Maria Gonzalez

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@vectorpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mixed-mode endpoint: first-token and sustained throughput carveout for VectorPay pilot

Maria — thanks, good questions. Answering inline and attaching the formal carveout language.

1) Observable TTFT: our numbers are measured end-to-end (client TCP/RPC -> first token delivered). The streaming TTFT target of 150 ms is median observed to your region on Dedicated pools; for non-streaming we quote 700-900 ms to first token visible to the client (this is the number you'll see in your client telemetry). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 in the canary.

2) Sustained emission and concurrency: the 100-140 tok/s range for non-streaming is per-request once generation begins under typical concurrency. Under high concurrency (50+ concurrent long requests) you should expect request pacing and kernel-level multiplexing that can lower per-request token/sec; that is why we specify a sustained target for the non-streaming path but do not guarantee absolute per-request token/sec at extreme concurrency without a dedicated capacity commitment.

Proposed formal carveout language (attached): redwood-sla-exception-form.xlsx, sheet "MixedModeClause" — key points summarized below:
- Streaming (<=512 tokens): TTFT median 150 ms (goal), p95 <= 400 ms. No sustained per-request throughput guarantee; design for interactive flows.
- Non-streaming (>=512 tokens): initial first-token <= 900 ms (p50 target 800 ms), sustained emission 100-140 tok/s per request under normal concurrency (<30 concurrent long requests).
- Canary: 14-day canary, telemetry collection (p50/p95/p99 TTFT, errors, token/sec distributions). Pass criteria: p95 TTFT within 1.5x of targets and error rate <0.5% for long completions.
- Pricing: mixed-mode carveout triggers a temporary 8% price uplift on token consumption during the canary for capacity reservation; thereafter normal committed pricing applies pending Dedicated reservation.

Action items for VectorPay:
- Confirm you accept the mixed-mode clause and canary constraints or provide redlines.
- Share legal contact for a fast-track review (we can exchange redlines in DocuSign/SharePoint).

If helpful, Karthik (cc'd) can run a short tech session to walk infra through what triggers the non-streaming fallback.

Ben

Maria — quick technical follow-up and proposed timeline from infra side.

- Triggering non-streaming fallback: we use request-length heuristics (>=512 tokens) and complexity signals (presence of heavy decoding constraints). It is deterministic in the SDK and we can expose a header so VectorPay can force a sync path for specific requests for testing.
- Canary timeline: we recommend starting the 14-day canary on Mon 2/23. We'll limit to a max of 1M tokens/day across the pilot and schedule daily telemetry sync (15 minutes) with your SRE team.
- Pricing note: as Ben mentioned, there will be an 8% uplift during the canary to reserve capacity for long-generation workloads. After successful canary, we'll convert to committed Dedicated pricing (if you opt in) or revert to standard PAYG pricing.

If you can confirm legal contact and whether you want us to open a DocuSign envelope with the mixed-mode clause, we can move quickly.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Technical Lead, Infra Integrations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

- The canary daily cap can stay 1M tokens/day but please add a short overlap window (48 hours) at the start where we can run targeted stress tests at 1.5x expected concurrency.

Legal contact: legal@vectorpay.com — please open a DocuSign with the MixedModeClause and the 48-hr stress window addition.

Once we have DocuSign we can sign and kick off the canary on 2/23. Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Maria
